records.mutation: intersect constraints across live readings instead of rejecting each reading alone, and ban recalled-puzzle values and smallest/looks-intended picks
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent hint scored 0/8, with 3 of 8 truncating at the token cap and the rest running past 13k tokens; every rollout enumerated the divisor pairs, correctly saw that a speaker's own value pins the partner inside one reading, then judged each reading separately, declared both impossible, and finally emitted either the smallest divisor, a divisor chosen because it 'looks intended', or a value it admitted was only recalled from a similar classic puzzle. The incumbent names the label ambiguity but still has the student test readings one at a time, and its ban on unverified boxing is too weak to stop plausibility and memory picks, so I made the intersect-across-live-readings rule explicit and closed both guessing routes.

records.mutation: target the root-cause arithmetic slip: state the conjugate rule for complex division and that a reciprocal inverts the modulus, replacing the generic no-restart advice's reliance on the student catching its own error
records.subagent_summary: Seven of eight fresh rollouts were correct in 5.7k-9.1k tokens; the lone failure derived the correct locus and center/radius quickly, then evaluated one reciprocal of a purely imaginary number by keeping the modulus instead of inverting it, so its own spot-check disagreed and it re-audited the sound derivation dozens of times until the 16384-token cap, never stating a result. Rounds 5 and 6 tried to bound the rechecking loop and both lost train and transfer, so instead of managing the loop I attack what triggers it: name the conjugate procedure and the modulus-inversion fact for complex division, which is a reusable arithmetic guard, while keeping the incumbent's setup, no-restart rule, symmetry shortcut, and early commitment.

records.mutation: add a tie-break rule for conflicting candidate values (resolve numerically, do not default to the newest) plus reserve-tokens-to-report discipline
records.subagent_summary: Four of eight rollouts scored; every one of the four failures hit the 16384-token cap, so the incumbent's wedge and symmetry advice is working and is kept verbatim. All eight reached a candidate value inside the first ~7k characters yet kept re-testing rotations for another ~50k; crucially one failure drifted to a different overlap value late and committed to it, and one never closed its reasoning block at all, so this revision adds an explicit conflict rule (adjudicate two competing values by one numeric configuration rather than trusting the most recent pass) and an instruction to reserve budget so the value actually reaches the visible reply.

records.mutation: add a fencepost guard: the summed root budget counts the items, not the gaps between them, so do not add one
records.subagent_summary: 4 of 8 fresh rollouts were correct, and the incumbent's residual-root framing is now landing: three failures reached the summed per-piece budget but then miscounted units, one adding one for a fencepost by treating the budget as bounding gaps rather than items. The two remaining failures reverted to the old traps of equating the cap with the piece count or declaring the setup impossible because one piece cannot step by a constant, so the revision keeps the pointwise-residual and reusability language intact and adds only a compact off-by-one guard tying the budget to the quantity actually requested.

records.mutation: add a contradiction-triage clause: blame your own rewrite, spot-check that single step, never declare the problem faulty
records.subagent_summary: Seven of eight fresh rollouts were correct in 8-11k tokens; the single failure lost a sign while dividing across a base-1/2 logarithm, reached a negative discriminant, and then spent the remaining ~10k tokens to the cap re-deriving the same reduction, reinterpreting the given vector condition, and finally asserting the problem was mistyped instead of rechecking the one rewrite it had just performed. The incumbent's discard clause covers bad roots but says nothing about what to do when no root exists, so I added a transferable triage rule that localizes the blame to the last algebraic rewrite and forbids concluding the statement is faulty, which is a generic non-termination trigger rather than anything specific to this setup.

records.mutation: add the LIFO orientation fact (a destination's bottom is its earliest arrival) and force the which-item-in-slot-k part to be enumerated over the shared free-choice atoms instead of priced as 1/n
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent gave 1/8; six rollouts terminated normally at 10k-15k tokens and two hit the cap while relitigating, so length is secondary. Seven of the eight failures reached the free-choice atom count on the first part but then abandoned that sample space on the later part, asserting that every item is equally likely in every slot and reading off 1/n, and most of those also equated the requested bottom slot with the item moved last. The revision keeps the shared-sample-space and symmetry-trap framing that has transferred best, adds the last-in-first-out orientation fact that a destination's bottom is its earliest arrival, and demands the which-item-in-slot-k event be written as a move-sequence constraint and enumerated over the same atoms.

records.mutation: add alternating-sign pattern cue, single-entry arithmetic repair, and a ban on the long from-scratch rewrite that burns the budget
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling under the incumbent scored 2 of 8; all six failures ran to the 16384-token cap. Two distinct budget sinks were visible: one rollout had already derived the correct signed pattern from small cases and then began rewriting the entire solution from scratch, running out of tokens mid-restatement, while others abandoned verified small-case values to chase a polynomial reinterpretation and got stuck expanding a long product to extract one low-order coefficient. The revision therefore names the alternating-sign / factorial-denominator shape to look for, tells the student to repair a single deviant entry's arithmetic instead of retheorizing, demotes the polynomial recast to an abortable cross-check, and explicitly forbids the terminal from-scratch rewrite.

records.mutation: keep the incumbent's opening scaffold verbatim, drop the vague integrality/units tail, and replace it with a compact transferable rule: use integrality/divisibility as the pinning constraint rather than trial values, then recompute once by a second route
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored reward 1 and stopped cleanly at 2.7-4.9k completion tokens, so train_i is saturated at 1.0 and every remaining point of J must come from transfer. The traces show the useful reusable move is exactly the divisibility lever (13-21 mentions of the common-divisor argument each) while the incumbent's final clause about checking integrality and units is never acted on and instead coincides with 22-59 repeated re-readings of scope per trace; prior rounds also showed that rewriting the opening sentences collapses train while long appends only diluted transfer. So this round keeps the opening verbatim, deletes the unused tail rather than appending to it, and substitutes one short domain-neutral statement of the divisibility-as-constraint technique plus a single independent recheck.

records.mutation: harden the sum-and-difference step against dropping the numeric right-hand sides and add a general no-symmetry fallback (convenient substitutions plus unknown/equation counting) so the hint still gives usable guidance when no shared-center structure exists
records.subagent_summary: Seven of eight fresh rollouts were correct and finished well under the cap; the lone failure reached the shared-center antisymmetric form correctly, then mishandled the add-the-two-values step by discarding the numeric right-hand sides, read the resulting degenerate center as proof the whole structure was impossible, and burned the remaining budget on full coefficient expansion of the composition. The revision therefore makes carrying those numbers explicit and reclassifies a degenerate center as a one-line repair, and spends the freed tokens on a general fallback so the hint remains actionable on problems with no such symmetry rather than only on this narrow pattern.

records.mutation: replace whole-map construction with single-item orbit tracing, ban untraced product-of-swaps period claims, and add a tie-break rule to run one extra size when the exponent is ambiguous
records.subagent_summary: Only 1 of 8 rollouts scored and 5 hit the 16384-token cap; every failure tried to construct the full position map by hand, produced a non-bijective or self-contradictory table, and then either asserted period 2 from product-of-disjoint-swaps talk it never iterated or oscillated between two neighbouring powers of the size parameter until the budget ran out. The revision therefore redirects effort from map-building to tracing one item until it returns, forbids reading a period off untraced cycle vocabulary, and tells the student to resolve an ambiguous exponent by working one more size instead of guessing.
